newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B index ends up on speculative buying.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B index ends up on speculative buying.

text.p: Shanghai's B share index ended sharply up on Tuesday on speculative buying by institutions wanting to boost the price of shares in which they have large holdings, brokers said.
The index surged 3.332 points or 3.92 percent to 88.291 points on volume of 15.245 million shares worth $11.209 million.

Brokers said domestic institutions which suffered losses in last week's market falls pushed up stocks in firms which have a heavy weighting on the index, triggering some follow-up buying from retail investors.
"Some domestic institutions do not want to let the market fall because they hold large positions and need follow-up buying to create an opportunity for liquidation," one broker said.
"But market sentiment is still cautious amid talk of possible further crackdown measures from Beijing before too long," he said.
"The short-term market momentum mainly depends on the A share performance, as domestic investors have become a major force on the B share market," another broker said.
Of 43 B shares, 40 traded, with 35 up, two flat and three down.
Shanghai Posts & Telecommunications Equipment was the star on speculative buying, surging $0.048 or 9.95 percent to $0.530 on volume of 175,500 shares.

The market barometer Shanghai Lujiazui Finance and Trade Zone Development was the most actively traded on some institutional support, rising $0.060 or 4.13 percent to $1.510 on volume of 2.3 million shares.
Shanghai's A share index continued its rebound on institutional buying in blue chips, but trading remained cautious amid market uncertainties in the short term, brokers said.
The index rose 37.746 points or 2.68 percent to 1,444.218 points on volume of 497.0 million shares worth 7.2 billion yuan.
The SSE30 blue chip index jumped 179.531 points or 4.58 percent to 4,101.820 points.

Shanghai Fello Acoustics Co was the star on news that its biggest shareholder had increased its holdings through purchases on the A share market, surging 1.16 yuan or 10.00 percent to 12.75 yuan on volume of 1.5 million shares.
